jobDescription: Wrenfield Hotels runs 30 mid-scale hotels. The Implementation Project Manager leads property-system projects across the estate: planning, vendor coordination, data migration, staff training and cut-over into live operation at each hotel, with signed go-live approval and a stabilisation period before handover to IT support. The role manages its own project budget and reports variances to the IT director. Most of the hotels have between 80 and 150 rooms, each with a general manager and a duty-manager team, and property systems are supported by a small central IT team.
requirements: Plans multi-property system projects with a schedule and dependency log.
Coordinates data migration with vendors and checks the migrated records.
Has led a system cut-over into live operation at multiple properties, with signed go-live approval and a stabilisation period.
Manages a project budget and reports variances.

evidence.text: Systems Project Manager, Lindqvist Hotel Group, June 2020 to August 2024: planned the replacement of the property management system across 12 hotels in three waves, with a schedule and a dependency log shared with the vendor, plus a readiness checklist for each wave.

Coordinated the migration of guest profiles and future reservations with the vendor and ran reconciliation checks on record counts and deposit balances before each wave, signing off each reconciliation with the vendor.
Cut each wave over to the new property management system overnight, the last of the 12 hotels going live on 29 January 2024, and ran a two-week stabilisation desk after each wave.
Organised front-desk and reservations training in a training copy of the new system, preloaded with practice bookings for each hotel, with sessions timed around shift patterns.
Kept the hardware and training lines of the project budget; the IT director held the overall budget. Reported spend on those two lines to the IT director each month.

Work sample: the wave-three cut-over plan, with the overnight timeline, the reconciliation checklist, a fallback decision point at 04:00 and the contact list for the vendor and the hotels' duty managers, plus the go or no-go criteria for the fallback point.

HR verification note: the former employer supplied the signed go-live certificates for all three waves; each names the candidate as project manager, and the wave-three certificate is dated 30 January 2024, the morning after the final overnight switch.
Recruiter logistics note: the candidate can travel to properties up to three nights a week and is available from mid-November.
